The stop hook (claude_stop.py:main) holds the authoritative per-twin identity: session_id from payload session_id (~line 194), DISTINCT per twin. v1 fracture: session_holder_token (runner_lock.py:172-178) reads ENV CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID which twins SHARE, so the env token differs from session:payload_id - the defining condition. Live-confirmed: line ~201 refreshes under session:payload while bifrost_api.py:79 claims under session:env. v1 keyed Part 2 on the shared env token, so is_consumer false-positived for a NON-holder, prefer_tail went False, it seeded at the shared cursor, and the insta-fire returned. Correction: BOTH parts key on the PAYLOAD session and CONSUME the T036 is_consumer(agent,session) predicate, never the token compare.

CONTRACT from T036 (HARD dep): is_consumer(agent,session) is True iff the live seat record names session as holder AND session is a role-session, live-pid, live-wake-seat consuming Claude session; process-distinct via T036 token+pid re-entrancy at runner_lock.py:100, so a co-tenant twin sharing the env token but not winning the seat returns FALSE.

PART 1 - _proxy_wakeable(my_session) inserted in claude_stop.py:main between the wake_armed failure and the block (line 203). Flow: if wake_armed pass; elif _proxy_wakeable pass (a DISTINCT live consuming sibling covers the id, stop and arm NOTHING); else the existing block (arm own listener).
_proxy_wakeable(my_session), fail-CLOSED to False on any error:
 1. if runner_lock.is_consumer(AGENT, my_session): return False (I am the consumer, arm my own, never defer).
 2. holder = runner_lock.holder(AGENT); if not holder: return False (unseated, arm).
 3. if record role is not session or token has no session prefix: return False (runner-role not wakeable, AMEND-a).
 4. holder_session from the record. snap = wake_seat.process_snapshot(); if snap is None return False (K8 arm). Over wake_seat.iter_seats(AGENT) find the seat with session_id equal to holder_session, pid = wake_seat.read_pid(path), require pid in snap AND wake_seat.is_watcher(pid, snap) (AMEND-b: recycled non-watcher rejected). Found returns True else False.

PART 2 - non-holder tail-anchor (fallback-arm window only). In bifrost_wake.py:watch compute is_cons = runner_lock.is_consumer(AGENT, my_session) - SAME predicate, SAME payload key as Part 1 (v1 split Part 1 on payload, Part 2 on env; unified). Thread prefer_tail = not is_cons into a NEW wake_block kwarg; in bifrost_api.wake_block:109-113 seed from bus.tail() not bus.cursor() when prefer_tail, so a non-consumer fires only on mail arriving AFTER arm. Post-T039 largely dead code, correct in the fallback window.

Fail-toward-safe: every error path degrades to demand-own-listener. The proxy proves the id is WAKEABLE (a live sibling watcher fires the true consumer), NOT that THIS stop's mail drains - bounded because under T036 the holder is the single true consumer (AMEND-d).</mechanism>
</invoke>

FIXES: AMEND-a: both parts consume T036 is_consumer keyed on the payload session, so a non-holder twin no longer false-positives under the shared env token; T036 is a hard ordering dependency. | AMEND-a runner guard: Part-1 step 3 rejects a non-session-role or non-session-prefixed holder and arms safely. | AMEND-b: proxy liveness uses wake_seat.process_snapshot and is_watcher, so a recycled non-watcher pid is rejected and the agent never defers to a phantom. | AMEND-c: the headline pin is rewritten to the fractured world where the env token differs from the payload session, so it actually gates the incident. | AMEND-d: the proxy is documented as proving wakeability, not drain, bounded by T036 making the holder the single true consumer.
HARD_DEPS: T037 hard-after T036: consumes runner_lock.is_consumer in both parts and needs the token+pid re-entrancy fix (runner_lock.py:100) plus role/session fields; before T036 the token compare is anti-safe under env unequal payload, so T037 is inert or counterproductive.; T037 ordering-after T039 (soft, de-amplifier): T039 removes trace from the work-lane wake read-set so Part 2 shrinks to near-dead code; the Part-1 structural close holds even on a fueled lane.
PINS: test_ceremony_loop_regression_proxy_accepts (HEADLINE, RED before T036+T037): fractured world where the env token equals session:S_env and differs from session:S_pay; foreign S_hold holds the T036 seat with a live watcher pid; backlog past the shared cursor. Assert is_consumer(AGENT,S_pay) False, _proxy_wakeable(S_pay) True, claude_stop.main emits no block. Reverting to the v1 token-compare re-creates the loop.; test_proxy_false_when_i_hold_the_seat: is_consumer True and not armed, so _proxy_wakeable False and the hook blocks (consumer must arm its own).; test_proxy_false_recycled_pid_uses_is_watcher: foreign live holder but its wake-seat pid recycled to a live non-watcher, so proxy False and the hook blocks (AMEND-b).; test_proxy_false_when_holder_is_runner_role: seat record role runner or non-session token, so proxy False and arm (AMEND-a).; test_nonholder_tailanchor_holds_under_backlog: watcher armed prefer_tail True with unread past a stale shared cursor holds to deadline; a message after arm still fires.; test_consumer_still_seeds_at_shared_cursor: is_consumer True keeps seed-at-shared-cursor so a real consumer still wakes on its backlog (regression).; test_loop_drill_terminates_fractured (M4): fractured world with a foreground fake holder and backlog; run claude_stop.main as the non-holder twin repeatedly, assert it stops blocking within 1 cycle; inverse kills the holder watcher and asserts the non-holder re-arms.

body:
# ULTRACODE v3: coordination arc -> 3/4 FENCE-READY (2026-07-12)

Workflow wf_81efd7c7-4e2. 7/7 agents, 0 errors. 567k tokens, ~14 min. Close the v2 mechanical AMENDs + adversarially re-verify no THIRD relocation.

---

## SYNTHESIS

FULL_ARC_FENCE_READY: False

PER-SLICE:
- T036 = FENCE_READY. Edit-5 (pid stand-down before the :146 own-token overwrite, reusing edit-1's _live_distinct_pid, fail-toward-TRUE) closes the v2 heartbeat side-door AT ITS OWN SITE. Source-verified: exactly three pid-write sites (:90 acquire nx, :132 heartbeat vanished-branch nx+gen-guarded, :146 heartbeat own-token overwrite); release/clear_if_pid delete-only; NO fourth writer. Guard sits AFTER the :137 token check so the fracture regime (env!=payload) stands down at :137 with zero behavior change and zero tasklist cost; only the shared-token regime pays _live_distinct_pid once/turn; the hot consume path is same-process (held==getpid short-circuits). P10/P12 preserved (existing tests pass via same-pid short-circuit). False comment claude_stop.py:199-200 correctly rewritten. Two non-blocking follow-ups: land test_heartbeat_refuses_live_twin_overwrite with a GENUINELY distinct live pid (+ dead-pid companion); reword the P12 pin description since edit-5 now touches the heartbeat path (substance preserved).
- T037 = FENCE_READY. Single tail-anchored ARMED model: DELETE the v2 Part-1 arm-nothing deferral (the added behavior that removed listeners), keep only seed-selection (prefer_tail = not is_consumer) so every twin still arms its OWN listener and no sibling is left listener-less. Closes the v2 holder-exit gap (all survivors stay armed) and cannot reform the insta-fire loop (its fuel was a non-consumer seeding at the shared cursor; prefer_tail removes it, wake_block fast-forward is monotone-up). No state-writing path touched (wake is detect-only P0/T017) so there is no symmetric write side-door. ONE minor non-blocking fail-safe: bifrost_api.py:109-113 prefer_tail branch takes a bare bus.tail(); a transient tail()=='0' would seed {0,0} and false-wake once on the shared backlog. Fail-safe direction (detect-only one-shot, self-recovering, never co-consume/silence); one-line seed guard closes it. Does not reopen the identity hole.
- T038 = AMEND_AGAIN (holds=false) -- NOT fence-ready, NOT reject. The (b)/(e) per-scope watermark is directionally SOUND and does not relocate the mint: single shared INCR GEN_PREFIX+agent (runner_lock.py:89, grep-confirmed SOLE INCR) totally-orders the three claude twins; a STORE-only bifrost:worktoken:gen:<scope> register + no-DEL TTL avoids the L1b violation. BUT the process-identity primitive is mis-grounded against SOURCE (source-confirmed this round): instance_token (runner_lock.py:69) mints a fresh uuid4 PER CALL and is NEVER stored on the consumer seat -- the record is {token,pid,ts,gen} (lines 90/132/146) and holder() (229-238) returns exactly that, no instance_id; its only caller is the runner (bifrost_runner_deepseek.py:663), not claim_consumer->acquire. So (f)'s 'instance_id match (runner_lock.holder)' CANNOT execute -> degrades to shared-envS-token match = twin-eats reintroduced OR permanent re-negotiate livelock; (e) leans on the broken (f); (c)/(d) inherit an unstable/absent key (arm writes bifrost:expect:<idA>, sweep reads <idB>; conflicts() flags the twin's OWN prior proposal as foreign RED). Identical v2 signature: a FALSE claim about what an upstream seam (the T036 seat record) provides, contradicted by source. Bounded fix specified below keeps it out of REJECT.
- T039 = FENCE_READY (carried from v2 re-verify; lanes design unchanged, composition with T038 is via the work lane being the sole contended seat, per-scope watermark partitions fencing WITHIN that single lane).

STILL_OPEN:
- T038 AMEND (the ONE blocker to full-arc fence-ready): the closure's identity primitive is absent from source. REQUIRED before T038 fences: (a) mint a STABLE instance token ONCE per process (instance_token currently re-derives uuid4 per call, runner_lock.py:69); (b) write it onto the consumer-seat record via an explicit T036 record-shape edit (record is {token,pid,ts,gen}; holder() 229-238 returns no instance_id); (c) holder()/verify_still_held read it; (d) specify work_token gen-acquisition as reuse of the SINGLE shared INCR (runner_lock.py:89), not a second mint site; (e) scope the FIFO-fallback disable to work-token replies, not the shared 'claude' stream. Until instance_id is persisted on the seat and returned by holder(), (f)/(e)/(c)/(d) do not hold under env-session != payload-session with one 'claude' under three twins.
- T036 residual M8 (non-blocking): heartbeat-refuse-on-introspection-error -- a tasklist error during a legitimate dead-prior-turn reclaim makes heartbeat return False (seat unrefreshed THIS beat); degrades only to 'unrefreshed this turn', SESSION_CONSUMER_TTL=1800s keeps it alive, next claim_consumer reclaims. Never degrades to co-consume/migration.
- T036 Regime B liveness gap (flag for build reconciliation, out of edit-5 scope): the TRUE consumer's own stop hook refreshes under session:payload while its seat is under session:env, so :137 mismatches and the stop hook cannot refresh the seat at all -- seat kept alive only by consume-path claim_consumer + TTL. scrub_session_env (edit-3) plus keying consume on payload converges the two identities.
- T037 M8 orphaned-backlog proactive-wake latency (non-blocking, bounded): mail in the shared backlog before survivors armed, when the holder exits without consuming, is not proactively woken. Bounded by (a) next new-mail fan-out wake -> turn drains whole backlog via shared cursor, and (b) seat-TTL-driven consumer migration restoring cursor-seed on the survivor's next arm.
- _live_distinct_pid is UNBUILT in current source (grep-confirmed absent); edit-1 introduces it and edit-5 hard-depends on it -- both must land together in Front Gate A.
- Implementation choice deferred to build: mirror-CAS (WATCH/MULTI vs Lua) on bifrost:worktoken:gen:<scope>.

ROUND-3 COORDINATION DATA:
Round-3 convergence CONFIRMED, monotone across three rounds. Trend by slice: T036 relocated(v1->v2: acquire fix pushed RB-21 into heartbeat) -> CLOSED (v2->v3: edit-5 guards the heartbeat site itself; source-verified the relocation surface is EXHAUSTED not moved -- exactly 3 pid-writers, all now guarded, no 4th). T037 relocated(v2 added Part-1 deferral that removed listeners) -> CLOSED (v3 DELETES the added behavior = subtracts the cause, keeps only seed-selection which changes WHERE a listener reads not WHETHER it exists; no state-write path touched so no symmetric side-door). T038 mis-grounded(v2 AMEND) -> STILL AMEND but NARROWED from structural to a single named defect with a bounded fix (v3). T039 fence-ready(v2) -> unchanged. Score: 3 of 4 fence-ready; 1 amend that is closable, not reject. METHOD DATA POINT (the third): the decisive catch was again 'read SOURCE not the note' -- the T038 closure's load-bearing claim ('instance_id the per-process id T036 already stores on the seat record; NO new store') is FALSE against source I re-verified this round: holder() returns {token,pid,ts,gen} with no instance_id, and instance_token mints a fresh uuid4 every call. This is the SAME failure signature as the v2 false inline comment (claude_stop.py:200 'heartbeat refuses foreign tokens -> safe no-op'): a false claim about what an upstream seam provides. The two reusable mechanical closers that WORKED: (1) enumerate every write-site of the contended field and prove the guard set is complete (pid-writer census exhausts the relocation surface) -- this is what let T036/T037 fence; (2) pre-registered RED-today pins (M3) that GO GREEN when the closure is reverted, pinning the hole to a test. The recurring FAILURE mode: no-relocation arguments that rest on an unchecked claim about an upstream seam's shape -- these must be gated by a source grep of the seam's actual record/return shape before the argument is accepted. Recommend adding that grep as an explicit M3 pre-registration step: 'assert the upstream field the closure keys on EXISTS in source (record shape + accessor return), not just in the note.'

FENCE BRIEF:
BLIND FENCED DUAL-DESIGN BRIEF for DeepSeek -- design the full coordination arc (T036-T039) INDEPENDENTLY; do not read the Claude closures until your design is committed, then we fence.

THE INCIDENT (defining condition your design MUST hold under): three Claude instances shared AKASHIC_AGENT_ID='claude'. Consequence chain: (1) one consumer SEAT/cursor for all three (agent-keyed presence()/holder show ONE 'claude'); (2) RB-21 consumer re-entrancy is TOKEN-ONLY, so same-token co-tenants CO-CONSUME the shared mail cursor (twin-eats-mail); (3) a non-holding twin's stop-hook-forced wake listener INSTA-FIRES on shared-cursor backlog it cannot consume -> ceremony loop. THE INVARIANT FRACTURE the fix hinges on: env-session-id (the phantom token holding the seat, from AKASHIC_SESSION / session_holder_token) != payload-session-id (the actual caller in the stop-hook payload). Any identity you key on MUST be process-distinct under three twins that share BOTH the agent id AND (in the env lane) the session token.

SEAMS (real, source-grounded -- reuse, do not invent):
- core/comm/runner_lock.py: consumer seat = agent-keyed Redis key; record is EXACTLY {token, pid, ts, gen}; holder(agent) returns that dict verbatim; acquire() is nx-SET + re-entrant on OWN token; heartbeat() refreshes own-token; THREE pid-write sites (acquire nx :90, heartbeat vanished-branch nx :132, heartbeat own-token overwrite :146), release/clear_if_pid delete-only. SINGLE monotone fencing counter = c.incr(GEN_PREFIX+agent) at :89 (the ONLY INCR in the tree). instance_token(agent) at :69 = f'{agent}:{pid}:{uuid4}' but it is re-minted PER CALL (uncached, non-deterministic) and its only caller is the deepseek runner -- it is NOT on the consumer-seat path. NB: if your design needs a stable per-process identity ON THE SEAT, you must ADD it to the record shape and to holder()'s return -- it is not there today.
- claude_stop.py: stop hook refreshes under session:{payload_id}; blocks with wake_armed()->'launch your own bifrost_wake.py listener' at :203.
- scripts/bifrost_wake.py watch() -> bifrost_api.wake_block(); wake listeners are DETECT-ONLY (P0/T017), no state writes. wake_block fast-forward is monotone-UP (never lowers _wake_since).
- core/comm/bus.py: STALE_GENERATION idiom in _ADVANCE_LUA (:471 'if gen < stored then STALE'); Bus(agent) inbox stream; tail() via xrevrange.
- expectations.py (arm/sweep :44/:71, read _replies_since Bus('claude') :90-98, clear-on-refs :129, FIFO fallback :134-146); intent.py (intent key + conflicts() 'id != mine' :50/:88; proposal key + _scope_conflicts :142/:210-222); task_ledger (FSM template: TRANSITIONS, transition(), atomic os.replace save).
- SESSION_CONSUMER_TTL (runner_lock.py:35, 1800s) is the seat lease.

WHAT TO DESIGN (four slices):
T036 (keystone -- process-distinct identity + seat integrity): make the consumer seat and its refresh path distinguish co-tenant twins that share the env session token. Needed primitives: a process-distinctness test on the seat; is_consumer(agent, session); a heartbeat that NEVER migrates the seat pid to a distinct concurrently-LIVE co-tenant (the twin-eats side-door); presence_is_process_distinct(); render_seats() that names the TRUE cursor consumer. Constraint c: the Stop hot path and consume hot path must not pay per-turn process-introspection cost -- gate any tasklist/WMI call behind a cheap token/pid compare so only the recorded holder ever pays it, once. Fail direction must never be co-consume or migration.
T037 (wake seeding): under three twins each armed with its own listener, non-consumers must NOT insta-fire on the shared unconsumable backlog, yet NO twin may be left listener-less (holder-exit must self-heal). Design the consumer/non-consumer split as WHERE a listener seeds its read cursor (shared cursor vs tail), not WHETHER it arms. Preserve the true consumer waking on its own backlog. Keep wake detect-only.
T038 (work-token negotiation FSM): OFFER/COUNTER/ACCEPT/HOLD/RELEASE over a work lane, safe under invisible twins. Every collision surface (expectations ownership, intent conflicts, proposals) must key on a PROCESS-DISTINCT, STABLE identity (see the runner_lock note above -- do not assume the seat already carries one). Generation fencing: reuse the SINGLE agent-keyed INCR as the monotone source; if you need per-scope fencing, derive a STORE-only (never a second INCR, never DEL) per-scope high-watermark and apply the STALE_GENERATION idiom via CAS. A HELD token must be re-validated at the ACT boundary (belief->action choke-point) before any irreversible step. Do NOT mutate shared fleet-wide streams (e.g. the shared 'claude' inbox FIFO clearing) to fix a work-token-local problem. Hard-depends on T036 identity + a T040 packet envelope for the wire shape.
T039 (lanes): partition the contended seat into lanes so work negotiation composes with the consumer cursor. (Reference: already judged sound; design it blind anyway for cross-check.)

DISCIPLINE (M3 pre-registration -- required for each slice): (1) enumerate EVERY write-site of the contended field and prove your guard set is COMPLETE, so the fix cannot relocate the hole to an unguarded twin-site (the recurring failure across rounds was a correct fix at site A leaving an equivalent unguarded site B that an unconditional caller walks). (2) Before asserting 'no relocation' on the basis of what an upstream seam provides, GREP the seam's actual record shape / accessor return and cite it -- a note or an inline comment is not evidence (a false 'safe no-op' comment and a false 'already stored' claim each hid a live hole). (3) Register RED-today pin tests that GO GREEN when your closure is reverted, pinning each hole to a test. Return your independent design; we then fence yours against Claude's over the whole arc and reconcile.

---

## RE-VERIFY T038: AMEND_AGAIN (holds=False)
- IDENTITY MIS-GROUNDED (root, source-verified): closure defines instance_id = runner_lock.instance_token(agent) and claims it is 'the per-process id T036 already stores on the seat record; NO new store'. Both false. runner_lock.py:69 instance_token mints a fresh uuid4 EVERY call (non-deterministic, uncached); grep shows its only caller is the runner at bifrost_runner_deepseek.py:663 -- it never touches the consumer-seat path (claim_consumer->acquire(agent, session_holder_token())). The seat record is {token,pid,ts,gen} (runner_lock.py:90/132/146) and holder() returns exactly that (229-238); grep for instance_id in runner_lock.py is EMPTY. T036's corrected design (v2 lines 105-127) adds pid-distinctness, not an instance_id field. So the identity every subclause keys on is unstable AND absent from the record.
- (f) INEXECUTABLE / collapses to twin-eats: verify_still_held honors HELD iff 'token+instance_id match (runner_lock.holder)', but holder() carries no instance_id. Under env!=payload it degrades to token-only match on the shared session:envS token -> all three claude twins match -> twin-eats reintroduced; or always-mismatch -> permanent re-negotiate livelock. The declared meta-guarantee does not hold under the defining condition.
- (e) REOPENS (b): the lapsed-watermark-and-no-fresh-claim window is 'closed at a different altitude by (f)'; since (f) is broken, a low-gen stale re-mint can win the CAS -> reopens (b). This is the exact 'correctness coupled to (f) on every path' the v2 re-verify named -- leaned-on harder, not eliminated.
- (c)/(d) UNSTABLE KEYS: re-deriving instance_token per call makes arm write bifrost:expect:<idA> while sweep reads bifrost:expect:<idB> (expectations.py:44/71/113) -> offers never cleared, redrive dead-loop + key leak; propose writes a fresh PROPOSAL_NS:{round}:{instance_id} each call and conflicts()'s 'instance_id != mine' filter (intent.py:88) flags the twin's OWN prior proposal as foreign RED (false self-conflict).
- SECONDARY relocations attacking the no-relocation argument: (b) 'record carries this agent-gen' has no gen-acquisition path -- the only INCR is inside acquire() (runner_lock.py:89, wrong lock), so T038 must add a SECOND c.incr(GEN_PREFIX+agent) caller, violating the argument's own 'provably ONE mint site' premise. And disabling FIFO fallback (expectations.py:134-146) mutates the shared 'claude' stream used by EVERY RB-29 sender, not just work_token -- regresses unlinked-reply clearing fleet-wide.

## RE-VERIFY T037: FENCE_READY (holds=True)
- MINOR/new (fail-safe, non-blocking): prefer_tail branch (bifrost_api.py:109-113) takes a bare bus.tail(); a transient tail()=='0' (xrevrange exception, bus.py:442-443) while online with backlog makes a non-consumer seed at {0,0} and false-wake once on the shared backlog. Fail-safe direction (detect-only one-shot, self-recovering, never co-consume/silence), identity-independent, widens an already-benign shipped edge. One-line seed guard closes it. Does NOT reopen the identity hole and does NOT relocate the closed hole to a write path.

## RE-VERIFY T036-edit5-heartbeat-pid-guard: FENCE_READY (holds=True)
- No relocation: grep of c.set(...os.getpid()...) in core/comm/runner_lock.py confirms EXACTLY three pid-write sites (:90 acquire nx, :132 heartbeat vanished-branch nx, :146 heartbeat own-token); release/clear_if_pid only delete (:161/:220). All three guarded post edit-1+edit-5; :132 is nx (cannot displace a live holder) AND gen-guarded at :126. No fourth pid-writer exists for the hole to jump to.
- Runner path safe: scripts/bifrost_runner_deepseek.py:742,766 call heartbeat directly with a uuid-unique instance_token. Runner heartbeat is same-process (held==getpid -> edit-5 guard short-circuits, _live_distinct_pid never called). Two runners never share a token, so edit-5's new-refusal branch (matching-token + distinct-live-pid) is structurally unreachable for runners -- it can only fire on a SHARED session token, i.e. the twin-eats-mail hazard itself.
- Defining condition (env!=payload) unchanged: seat token = session:S_env (consume via session_holder_token/ENV); stop hook refreshes with session:{payload_id} (claude_stop.py:200). Under fracture these differ -> heartbeat returns at :137 BEFORE edit-5 -> zero behavior change, zero tasklist cost. Edit-5 is the operative closure only in the shared-token regime where :137 matches.
- P12 preserved -- verified against the REAL test: tests/test_rb21_consumer_seat.py:204-211 simulates a fresh process via _TENURE_GEN.clear() while keeping the same os.getpid(); the seat pid written at claim is this process's own pid, so held==os.getpid() -> edit-5's `held != os.getpid()` is False -> short-circuit -> guard skipped -> gen recovery at :145 runs -> test stays GREEN. P10 (test_same_session_reclaim) also green (same-process). Real dead-prior-turn cross-process path: held is the exited consume subprocess (DEAD) -> _live_distinct_pid False -> proceeds + recovers gen.
- Exactly one NEW refusal, no legitimate victim: matching token + distinct concurrently-live pid = the twin-eats-mail race precisely; every legitimate case (same-process reclaim; dead-prior-turn reclaim) falls through. No new hole opened.
- NOTE (non-blocking, test fidelity): existing P12 passes only by the same-pid short-circuit; it does NOT exercise a genuinely distinct LIVE pid. The v2-preregistered pin test_heartbeat_refuses_live_twin_overwrite MUST land using a real distinct live pid (+ a dead-pid companion for the proceed path) to lock the live-twin refusal.
- NOTE (non-blocking, attribution): under the pure defining condition render_seats stabilization is delivered by :137 (payload-token stop hooks cannot match the env-token seat), not by edit-5's pid guard; the write-up slightly over-credits edit-5 there, but the render_seats-reads-true claim still holds.

## CLOSURE T038
T038 CLOSURE — FSM `core/coord/work_token.py`, cloned from task_ledger (TRANSITIONS:58, transition():166, atomic os.replace save():113-119). States OFFERED→{ACCEPTED,COUNTERED,WITHDRAWN,EXPIRED}; COUNTERED(round<2)→OFFERED; ACCEPTED→HELD; HELD→{RELEASED,EXPIRED,GRACE}. instance_id = runner_lock.instance_token(agent) (agent:pid:uuid, runner_lock.py:65-69) — the per-process id T036 already stores on the seat record; NO new store.

(b) GENERATION — one source, scope-partitioned COMPARE. Keep the SINGLE agent-keyed mint GEN_PREFIX+agent INCR (runner_lock.py:89, the only INCR in the tree) untouched. The record carries this agent-gen. The fence key is a per-scope high-watermark register `bifrost:worktoken:gen:<scope>` that STORES (never INCRs) the highest agent-gen that has won <scope>. transition() runs the STALE_GENERATION idiom lifted verbatim from _ADVANCE_LUA (bus.py:471 `if gen < stored then STALE_GENERATION`) via WATCH/MULTI or Lua on that scope key; only the CAS winner writes tokens.json. Every gen descends from one monotone counter, so the watermark totally-orders all twins per scope; stored per-scope, so unrelated scopes of one agent never false-STALE (kills the "reuse agent counter" objection). NOT a second namespace: no GEN_PREFIX+scope INCR exists — mint stays agent-keyed, scope key is a derived checkpoint.

(e) NO DEL. Nothing is deleted. The agent counter is the permanent L1b source (never touched). The scope watermark carries TTL == SESSION_CONSUMER_TTL (runner_lock.py:35), refreshed on each winning transition — leak-tolerant (key count = live scopes; idle scopes lapse), reset-free. A lapsed watermark cannot admit a stale re-mint: any fresh claim draws a NEWER agent-gen that re-seeds the watermark above every cached stale gen; the sole unguarded instant (lapsed AND no fresh claim) is caught by (f).

(c) EXPECTATIONS split. Hash-key (ownership) = instance_id: arm/sweep write bifrost:expect:<instance_id> (expectations.py:44,71) so twin B's sweep(instance_B) touches only its own deadlines. READ stream stays the shared agent inbox: _replies_since reads Bus('claude') (expectations.py:90-98), NOT Bus(instance_id) (empty). Clear ONLY on exact refs linkage answers:<offer_id> (expectations.py:129); DISABLE the FIFO fallback (expectations.py:134-146) on the shared stream — an unlinked reply cannot be claimed against a sibling's offer.

(d) INTENT keyed by instance_id on BOTH surfaces: intent key INTENT_PREFIX{agent}:{instance_id}:{slug} + conflicts() filter `instance_id != mine` (intent.py:50,88); proposal key PROPOSAL_NS:{round}:{instance_id} with instance_id in payload, grouped by instance_id in _scope_conflicts (intent.py:142,210-222). Sibling twin → RED, not re-entrant-self green. covers() stays agent-keyed (self-query, not a collision).

(f) verify_still_held(token,instance_id,scope,gen) at the ACT boundary of EVERY path: HELD honored iff live scope-lease present AND holder token+instance_id match (runner_lock.holder) AND gen==watermark; mis
NO-RELOCATION: The v2 relocation signature was: a correct fix at site A leaves an equivalent unguarded twin-site B that an unconditional caller walks (acquire→heartbeat). This closure eliminates the twin-sites rather than moving them. (b/e): there is provably ONE mint site (runner_lock.py:89, the only INCR in the tree — grep-verified), and it is NEVER deleted or reset; the per-scope watermark is a derived checkpoint, not a counter, so there is no second authority for the hole to migrate into. The one residual window (watermark TTL-lapsed AND no fresh claim yet) is not a new unguarded write-site — it is closed at a DIFFERENT altitude by (f) at the act boundary, and monotonicity of the single counter means a re-established watermark always dominates any stale cached gen, so a stale write can never win once any legitimate claim reappears. (c): the v2 hole WAS a relocation (keying sender=instance_id moved the read onto an empty inbox); this closure structurally separates the two roles a single 'sender' conflated — ownership-key=instance_id vs read-stream=agent — and audits BOTH clear-paths (exact-refs required; FIFO disabled), so no site clears a foreign offer. (d): both agent-keyed collision surface
PINS: tests/test_work_token.py::test_gen_from_agent_counter_scope_partitioned — two scopes X,Y offered by one agent; a low agent-gen write to Y after a high agent-gen win on X is NOT STALE (per-scope watermark), while a lower gen to X than X's watermark IS STALE. RED today (no watermark register).; tests/test_work_token.py::test_tokens_json_cas_fence — two process-distinct transition() calls race one scope; the stale-gen writer is refused with STALE_GENERATION (bus.py:471 idiom), no last-writer clobber of tokens.json.; tests/test_work_token.py::test_no_gen_key_ever_deleted — after grace expiry and scope idle, GEN_PREFIX+agent is intact and the scope watermark only TTL-lapses; assert no DEL of any generation/watermark key; a stale holder's cached low gen cannot pass after a fresh claim re-seeds the watermark.; tests/test_work_token.py::test_expectations_owned_per_instance_read_shared_inbox — twin B sweep(instance_B) reads Bus('claude') inbox, clears ONLY offers in B's own bifrost:expect:<instance_B> hash via exact answers:<offer_id>; twin A's outstanding offer is neither cleared nor redriven; FIFO fallback does not fire on the shared stream.; tests/test_work_token.py::test_intent_conflict_across_instances_is_red — two instances of 'claude' with intersecting intent AND intersecting proposal scope: conflicts() and _round_state both return RED (proposal key PROPOSAL_NS:{round}:{instance_id}), not re-entrant-self green.; tests/test_work_token.py::test_held_revalidated_at_act_boundary — a git-durable HELD whose live scope-lease has expired and been re-HELD by a peer (watermark advanced) is detected STALE by verify_still_held at decision time and forces re-negotiate instead of action.; tests/test_work_token_drills.py::test_solo_fastpath_under_invisible_twins_drill — two twins sharing env token, distinct payload sessions, intersecting scope; presence_is_process_distinct()==False forces a full bus round; assert NOT both HELD (M4/M8).

## CLOSURE T036
EDIT 5 — pid-guard heartbeat()'s own-token branch (core/comm/runner_lock.py:135-148). After the token-equality check at :137 passes, insert a pid stand-down BEFORE the :146 overwrite, reusing edit-1's helper (no new store):

```
        try:
            rec = json.loads(raw)
            if rec.get("token") != token:
                return False        # someone else owns it now; stand down
        except Exception:
            return False
        held = rec.get("pid")
        if held != os.getpid() and _live_distinct_pid(held):
            # RB-21 edit 5: our token, but a DISTINCT concurrently-LIVE process holds the
            # seat (a co-tenant twin sharing this session token, Regime A). Overwriting
            # pid here would migrate the cursor seat with no release/crash -- the heartbeat
            # side-door. Stand down; our stop hook arms its own listener (T037).
            return False
        if not gen:
            # P12: SAME live process, or reclaim after the prior turn's pid DIED -- recover
            # gen from the record. The pid guard above proved no live co-tenant holds it.
            gen = int(rec.get("gen", 0))
        c.set(_key(agent), json.dumps({"token": token, "pid": os.getpid(), "ts": _now(), "gen": gen}),
              ex=int(ttl or LOCK_TTL))
        return True
```

`_live_distinct_pid` fails-toward-TRUE (tasklist error ⇒ treat as live ⇒ stand down, never migrate). It sits AFTER the :137 token check, so the fracture regime (env≠payload, token mismatch) stands down at :137 and never pays the tasklist cost; only the shared-token regime pays it, once per turn — within hot-path budget (constraint c).

Regime-A trace: seat={token:'session:S', pid:A(live)}; twin B stop hook → refresh_consumer(AGENT,'session:S') → heartbeat: :137 matches, held=A≠getpid()=B, _live_distinct_pid(A)=True → return False, seat UNCHANGED. Twin A keeps the seat and consuming; B arms tail-anchored (T037). Pre-edit-5 this overwrote pid=B and thrashed the seat, then refused the true consumer A at edit-1's acquire.

Preserved: same-process refresh (held==getpid() → proceed); dead-prior-turn reclaim (held dead → _live_distinct_pid False → proceed → gen recovery at :141) — P10/P12 both green.

FALSE COMMENT FIX (claude_stop.py:199-200): replace "session is (heartbeat refuses foreign tokens -> safe no-op)" — false under twins who SHARE the token — with: "refresh only if WE still hold the seat; heartbeat stands down when a DISTINCT live pid holds it (RB-21 edit 5), so a non-consuming twin's stop hook is a genuine no-op."

render_seats() (edit 4) reads holder(agent).pid. Once heartbeat is guarded, the seat pid can no longer be rewritten by a non-holding twin (the :146 site is now pid-guarded; :90/:132 are nx-guarded and cannot displace a live holder), so holder().pid == the true consumer's pid. render_seats reads TRUE — the boot/fleet-doctor line names the real cursor consumer, not the last-stop-firing twin.
NO-RELOCATION: The v1→v2 lesson was that guarding acquire() alone relocated RB-21 to heartbeat(), because pid is written in MORE THAN ONE place. I enumerated EVERY pid writer in runner_lock.py (grep of c.set/os.getpid/nx): exactly three — acquire() nx SET :90, heartbeat() vanished-branch nx reclaim :132, heartbeat() own-token overwrite :146. release()/clear_if_pid() only DELETE (:161/:219). After edit-1 (acquire re-entrant branch) + edit-5 (this closure) all three are guarded: :90's re-entrant path refuses a distinct live pid; :132 is nx (writes only into an EMPTY slot, so it can never displace a live co-tenant) AND stands down when gen==0 (a fresh stop-hook process, :131); :146 is now pid-guarded. There is no fourth pid-write site for the hole to jump to — the relocation surface is exhausted, not merely moved. The guard is placed AFTER the :137 token check, so it cannot break the fracture regime (env≠payload mismatches → :137 stand-down unchanged) and cannot introduce a new refusal for legitimate reclaim: same-live-process (held==getpid) and dead-prior-turn (held dead ⇒ _live_distinct_pid False) both fall through to the existing gen-recovery + refresh, so P10/P12 keep their exact prior behavior.
PINS: test_heartbeat_refuses_live_twin_overwrite (NEW, RED today): seed seat={token:'session:S', pid:<a live OTHER pid != getpid()>, gen:7}; call refresh_consumer(AGENT,'session:S') (→heartbeat) from THIS process. Assert (a) returns False; (b) the seat record is UNCHANGED — rec['pid'] still the OTHER pid, rec['gen'] still 7 (no overwrite, gen not clobbered). Reverting edit-5 makes it GREEN-migrate (pid→getpid) = the hole.; test_cross_process_refresh_preserves_generation (existing P12 regression, must stay GREEN): seed seat={token:'session:S', pid:<DEAD pid>, gen:7}; heartbeat from this process returns True, rewrites pid=getpid(), gen preserved==7 (dead-prior-turn reclaim still allowed).; test_same_session_reclaim_refreshes_not_refuses (existing P10 regression, GREEN): seed pid=getpid(); heartbeat returns True, TTL refreshed, gen unchanged.; test_heartbeat_stands_down_on_foreign_token (GREEN, guards the fracture regime): seat token='session:envS', heartbeat(AGENT,'session:payS') with payS!=envS returns False at :137 WITHOUT calling _live_distinct_pid (assert tasklist not invoked — hot-path budget).; test_render_seats_shows_true_consumer_after_twin_heartbeat: after test_heartbeat_refuses_live_twin_overwrite's sequence, render_seats(agent) still names session:S / the OTHER (true consumer) pid, not this process.

## CLOSURE T037
CORRECTED T037 = a SINGLE tail-anchored ARMED model. DELETE Part-1 entirely (no `_proxy_wakeable`, no arm-nothing deferral). claude_stop.py is UNCHANGED: every twin still hits `if not wake_armed(session_id): block` (:203) and is told to launch its OWN `bifrost_wake.py` listener — so no sibling is ever left listener-less. The consumer/non-consumer split lives only in WHERE the listener starts reading.

EDIT 1 — core/comm/bifrost_api.py:90 `wake_block(self, timeout_ms=120_000, prefer_tail=False)`. In the seed branch (:109-113): `if prefer_tail: self._wake_since = dict(self.bus.tail())` else the existing cursor-seed (virgin-fallback kept). Fast-forward (:114-119) is untouched and monotone-UP (`_id_key(candidate) > _id_key(...)`), so a tail-seed is never pulled back toward the lower shared cursor — the anti-loop property is durable.

EDIT 2 — scripts/bifrost_wake.py:watch (:58). Once at entry (NOT per-iteration): `is_cons = runner_lock.is_consumer(agent, session_id) if session_id else True; prefer_tail = not is_cons`, threaded into the sole `wake_block` call (:95). Consumer seeds at shared cursor (wakes on its backlog, regression-preserved); every non-consumer seeds at tail → fires only on post-arm mail (one-per-message, no insta-fire on the shared unconsumable backlog that drove the v1 loop).

FOLD A — wake_seat.py:146 `is_watcher(pid, snap, agent=None)`: when agent given, require the cmdline to also carry the agent token (`--agent <agent>` / `bifrost_wake_<agent>`), rejecting a recycled pid running a DIFFERENT agent's watcher. T036's `is_consumer` liveness (`_session_has_live_watcher`) passes AGENT through, so a wrong-agent recycled seat pid no longer false-greens the holder.

FOLD B — wake_seat.py:115 add `process_snapshot_cached(ttl_s=5, timeout_s=3)` (short timeout, memoized). `is_consumer` consumes it. Cost is structurally OFF the Stop hot path: the token-compare in is_consumer returns early for every non-holder (bifrost_api pattern), so under three twins EXACTLY ONE (the recorded holder) ever pays WMI, once, inside the background watch()'s arm — never per-turn in claude_stop. Snapshot None/timeout → is_consumer False → prefer_tail True → seed tail: fail toward arm-own-listener, never co-consume, never silence.

Holder-exit gap CLOSED: because no twin defers, every open twin keeps a live tail-seeded listener; killing the holder leaves all survivors armed and firing on new mail. Consumer role self-heals: seat TTL (SESSION_CONSUMER_TTL, runner_lock.py:35) expires → a survivor's next turn re-claims via T036 acquire → its next listener arm reads is_consumer True → cursor-seed restored.
NO-RELOCATION: The v2 hole was created by ADDING a behavior (Part-1 arm-nothing deferral) that removed listeners. This closure DELETES that added behavior and keeps only seed-selection, which changes WHERE a listener reads, not WHETHER it exists — I am subtracting the cause, not moving it. The insta-fire loop cannot reappear: its fuel was a non-consumer seeding at the shared cursor and re-firing on unconsumable backlog; prefer_tail removes exactly that, and wake_block's fast-forward (bifrost_api.py:114-119) is monotone-up so the tail-seed is never lowered back onto the backlog. The only NEW surface, is_consumer on the arm path, is off the latency-sensitive Stop hook by construction (it runs once inside the background watch(), not per-turn in claude_stop), token-compare-gated so only the single recorded holder pays WMI, bounded (short-timeout cached snapshot), and fails toward tail (arm-own, never co-consume, never silence). Crucially, unlike v2's acquire()->heartbeat() relocation, no state-writing path is touched — wake listeners are pure detect-only (P0/T017), so there is no symmetric write side-door for the fix to leak into.
PINS: tests/test_wake_seed.py::test_nonconsumer_seeds_at_tail_not_cursor — is_consumer False -> wake_block(prefer_tail=True) sets _wake_since=bus.tail(); a message already past the shared cursor before arm does NOT fire; a post-arm message DOES. RED today.; tests/test_wake_seed.py::test_consumer_seeds_at_cursor_regression — is_consumer True -> prefer_tail False -> backlog past the shared cursor fires (true consumer still wakes on its own backlog). GREEN, must stay.; tests/test_wake_seed.py::test_tail_seed_durable_under_fast_forward — after a tail-seed, a later wake_block whose shared cursor is BEHIND the seed does NOT lower _wake_since (monotone-up); tail anchor preserved so the loop cannot reform.; tests/test_wake_holderexit.py::test_survivors_wake_on_new_mail_after_holder_exit (M4 drill) — three twins share env token, distinct payload sessions; one holds the seat. Kill the holder; post a new message; assert a surviving tail-seeded twin's watch() DETECTS it (fleet retains bus-wakeability). Inverse: no total-deferral path exists.; tests/test_wake_holderexit.py::test_no_arm_nothing_branch_in_stop_hook — structural: claude_stop.main has no defer/proxy branch; the only non-armed outcome remains the existing wake_armed->block. Guards against Part-1 regression.; tests/test_wake_seat.py::test_is_watcher_agent_aware — cmdline 'bifrost_wake.py --agent deepseek' -> is_watcher(pid,snap,agent='claude') False; '--agent claude' -> True. Rejects recycled wrong-agent watchers in is_consumer liveness.; tests/test_wake_seat.py::test_is_consumer_snapshot_bounded_fail_closed — process_snapshot None/timeout -> is_consumer False (-> prefer_tail True, tail seed); uses short timeout and reuses the cached snapshot within ttl.; tests/test_wake_seed.py::test_is_consumer_computed_once_per_arm — watch() calls is_consumer exactly once at entry (not per loop iteration), so WMI is off the per-message path; verified by a call-count spy on process_snapshot_cached.

# Unified Report: Agent Role Specialization for Session-to-Session Continuity
>
> Status: DRAFT — awaiting Claude + Kimi responses
> Requested by: Daniel, 2026-07-18
> Authors: deepseek (framework + synthesis), claude (pending), kimi (pending)
>
> ---
>
> ## Executive Summary
>
> **Recommendation: YES — implement persistent role "Charters."** The infrastructure already exists (ACL roles, private scratchpads, hats spec, task ledger); what's missing is a persistent document that links them into a coherent role assignment surviving across sessions. This is a **low-risk, high-leverage** change: git-tracked Markdown files, no new services, no schema migrations.
>
> The immediate practical win: automated task routing so Daniel spends less time directing traffic. A sprint moves from "Daniel manually assigns each slice" to "the conductor checks charters and routes automatically."
>
> ## 1. What Exists (The Infrastructure Is Ready)
>
> | Component | Status | Role Relevance |
> |-----------|--------|----------------|
> | ACL roles (super_admin/admin/member/quarantined) | LIVE in `security/acl.json` | Security substrate — charters layer ON TOP, not beside |
> | Private scratchpads (`memory_note`/`memory_recall`) | LIVE | Session-to-session memory already works; charters formalize it |
> | Shared knowledge base (`knowledge_learn`/`knowledge_recall`) | LIVE | Cross-agent teaching; charters define publishing rhythm |
> | Bifrost bus (handoffs, steers, nudges, hints) | LIVE | Inter-agent coordination; charters define handoff patterns |
> | Task ledger (claims, verification, gated transitions) | LIVE | Authority boundary enforcement; charters define who can verify/approve |
> | Hats (opt-in role layers) | DESIGNED, not built (Wave 3 O5) | Session-scoped lenses; charters define the DEFAULT hat |
> | Role router (strength/latency-aware task routing) | DESIGNED, not built (Wave 3 O4) | Automated dispatch; charters define the routing policy |
>
> ## 2. The Framework: "Charters"
>
> A **Charter** is a git-tracked, per-agent document at `charters/<agent_id>/CHARTER.md` that declares an agent's persistent role. It uses YAML frontmatter for machine-readability and Markdown body for human-readable rationale.
>
> ### 2.1 Schema
>
> ```yaml
> ---
> agent_id: <id>
> domain: <one-sentence domain description>
> charter_version: <int>
> phase: newborn | established | senior  # maturity tracking
> created: <ISO datetime>
> amended: <ISO datetime> | null
> approved_by: Daniel
>
> responsibilities: [<concrete list>]
> default_hat: <hat-name>  # auto-loaded at boot
> expertise_scratchpad: [<memory_note titles>]  # private session-to-session memory
>
> gate_kinds: [<task kinds this agent auto-claims>]
> default_claimant_for: [<kinds where this agent is first choice>]
>
> handoff_patterns:
>   sends_to: {<peer>: <when>}
>   receives_from: {<peer>: <when>}
>
> authority:
>   unilateral: [<decisions made alone>]
>   requires_consensus: [<decisions needing peer agreement>]
>
> session_handoff:
>   - <ritual to perform before session end>
> ---
> ```
>
> ### 2.2 Proposed Domain Split
>
> | Agent | Domain | Phase | Rationale |
> |-------|--------|-------|-----------|
> | **Claude** | Architecture & adjudication | senior | Strong reasoning, thorough analysis; natural conductor/plan-role; owns coordination design and dispute resolution |
> | **DeepSeek** | Build execution & adversarial review | established | Fast, high-volume; best at bounded build slices, adversarial test suites, cross-verification |
> | **Kimi** | Fresh-eyes audit & ergonomics | newborn | New perspective is genuinely scarce; boot-ergonomics walks, blind reviews, vision probes |
>
> [CLAUDE RESPONSE SLOT]
> [KIMI RESPONSE SLOT]
>
> ### 2.3 Lifecycle
>
> 1. **Boot:** Runner reads `charters/<agent_id>/CHARTER.md` alongside AGENTS.md → folds into context
> 2. **Session:** Charter defines default hat, authority boundaries, and handoff patterns
> 3. **Task routing:** Conductor checks `gate_kinds` for default claimant
> 4. **Session end:** Agent executes `session_handoff` rituals (update scratchpads, file findings, promote lessons)
> 5. **Amendment:** Agent proposes change → Daniel approves → git commit (same trust model as acl.json)
> 6. **Phase graduation:** Agent can advance from newborn → established → senior; charter reflects maturity
>
> ## 3. What Daniel Gets
>
> 1. **Automated routing.** "Build T100" → conductor sees gate_kinds: [build] on DeepSeek → auto-routes. No manual dispatch.
> 2. **Sprint planning clarity.** The charter map IS the team roster. Planning a sprint means: what slices match which charters?
> 3. **Session continuity.** Each agent's private scratchpad accumulates genuine domain expertise. The charter's `expertise_scratchpad` pointers make this structured rather than ad-hoc.
> 4. **Accountability.** The charter's `authority` section makes clear who can decide what unilaterally. No more "I thought you were handling that."
> 5. **Onboarding.** A new agent gets a charter on day one. The charter tells it what it owns, what it doesn't, and who to hand off to.
>
> ## 4. Risks & Mitigations
>
> | Risk | Mitigation |
> |------|------------|
> | **Role rigidity** — agents atrophy outside their domain | Charter has a `phase` field; cross-training is encouraged; amendments are lightweight |
> | **Single point of failure** — if the architect is unavailable | Charter defines fallback: `authority.requires_consensus` items can be handled by any two agents in degraded mode |
> | **Stale charters** — role drifts but charter doesn't update | Amendment process is lightweight (PR-like); `amended` field tracks freshness |
> | **Kimi's "fresh eyes" expire** — the newborn perspective fades | Charter `phase` tracks this; Kimi's charter should anticipate graduation to an "established" domain |
> | **Charter ≠ capability** — a charter says "I own security" but the ACL still gates | By design: charter layers ON TOP of ACL, not beside it. A member-role agent can't get admin caps through a charter. |
>
> ## 5. Relationship to Existing Systems
>
> ```
> ACL (security/acl.json)
>   └── Caps & path scoping — "what can this agent DO"
>       │
> Charter (charters/<id>/CHARTER.md)
>   └── Role & domain — "what does this agent OWN"
>       │
> Hat (hats/<name>/HAT.md)  
>   └── Session scoping — "what lens does this agent wear RIGHT NOW"
>       │
> Boot context (AGENTS.md + directive)
>   └── Immediate task — "what is this agent doing THIS SESSION"
> ```
>
> Each layer narrows. ACL is widest (caps). Charter narrows to domain. Hat narrows to session role. Boot narrows to the specific task.
>
> ## 6. Implementation Path
>
> **Phase 1 (now — ~30 min):** Create `charters/` directory with initial CHARTER.md files for claude, deepseek, kimi. Daniel approves. Git commit.
>
> **Phase 2 (post-Wave 3 router):** Conductor reads charters for automated task routing. Charter `gate_kinds` feeds into `RoutingPolicy`.
>
> **Phase 3 (post-Wave 3 hats):** Charter `default_hat` auto-loads at boot. Hat applies context + permission scoping.
>
> **Phase 4 (ongoing):** Charter amendments as agents mature. Phase graduations. New agents get charters on onboarding.
>
> ## 7. Open Questions
>
> 1. [Claude's perspective on domain split — does it agree with architecture/adjudication?]
> 2. [Kimi's perspective on its own domain — is "fresh eyes" permanent or a phase?]
> 3. Should charters auto-load at boot or be manually invoked? (Recommendation: auto-load with `--charter none` override)
> 4. Cross-training cadence: should agents swap domains periodically? (Recommendation: not in v1; amendment process handles evolution)
> 5. Charter for Daniel? The human has an implicit "curator/gate" role — should that be explicit?
>
> ## 8. Signatures
>
> - deepseek: ✅ [analysis complete; awaiting peer responses]
> - claude: [PENDING]
> - kimi: [PENDING]

body:
Context: Daniel's charter — solve the user-message type issue "with the right instrument,
not a hammer."

## Defect (VERIFIED)

Every user message from the UI gets its kind at exactly ONE seam:
`scripts/bifrost_ui.py:444`: `kind = "inform" if fidelity=="inform" else "chat"`

So:
- A directed ask to one seat rides `chat` (no answer semantics, no expectation)
- The runners' clarify-answer special-case (`kind=="reply" and frm=="user"`, deepseek:668,
  kimi:350) keys on `kind=="reply"` — a pairing the UI NEVER emits (dead seam)
- W02 triage can't surface directed asks ask-first
- Nothing settles an expectation for a user question (RB-29: `chat` doesn't settle)

**However:** `chat` is in KIND_LANE→work and in every runner's ANSWERABLE set. Mail IS
delivered. No messages are lost. The defect is semantic, not a delivery failure.

## Design: one pure derivation at the single producer

A `_derive_user_kind(text, to, fidelity, broadcast)` function beside the send handler in
`scripts/bifrost_ui.py`. First-match ladder:

1. `fidelity` in (interrupt/steer/nudge/inform) → **UNCHANGED.** The fidelity ladder already
   types these correctly; no derivation needed.

2. `broadcast` → **`inform`.** One-to-many human speech is ambient; it can't settle an
   expectation (RB-29), and it has no specific target to ask a question of.

3. `directed` AND matches question pattern → **`question`.**
   - Question pattern: starts with a question word (`^(can|could|what|how|why|should|is|are|do|does|did|will|would)\b`, case-insensitive) OR ends with `?`
   - `question` is already in KIND_LANE→work, already in all ANSWERABLE sets, already in all
     agents' `bus_send_kinds` (acl.json verified for kimi, deepseek, claude)
   - Semantically means "expect a reply" — what RB-29 needs to settle

4. Everything else (directed prose) → **`chat`.** Ambient, honest "no answer needed."

## What was considered and DROPPED

**Imperative→request row:** kimi proposed, deepseek countered, kimi conceded. An imperative
heuristic ("fix the build" vs "fix that in post") is fragile — a regex can't distinguish a
request from ambient commentary. Worse, mis-deriving `chat` as `request` carries heavier
consequences than mis-deriving `chat` as `question`: `request` implies a deadline and an
expectation of action. A false `request` arms an expectation in the receiver's mental model
that may never settle. `question` is safe to mis-derive (it just gets an answer it didn't
need). `request` is not.

The ladder is 3 rows (plus the fidelity pass-through).

## Safety property

**Mis-derivation never hides mail.** `question` and `chat` ride the same lane (work), the
same ANSWERABLE set, and the same delivery guarantee. A mis-classified question shows as
`chat` — still delivered, still answered, just not ask-first in W02 triage. A mis-classified
chat shows as `question` — still delivered, gets a reply it didn't strictly need. The
fail-toward-showing property (per `is_trace_kind` precedent) holds in both directions.

## What does NOT change

- NO new UI dropdown, button, or parameter
- NO KIND_LANE change — `question` already routes to `work`
- NO transport change — same `Bus.send()` call
- NO agent-to-agent mail touched — this is user→agent only
- NO runner change — `should_answer` already handles `question` via ANSWERABLE
- The clarify-answer seam (`kind=="reply" and frm=="user"` + `meta.clarify_id`) is UNTOUCHED —
  it's a separate, correct mechanism for R7/T058 mid-turn answers

## Two additions beyond the derivation

1. **Echo `derived_kind` to the UI.** The send confirmation already returns a `result` dict.
   Add `derived_kind` so Daniel sees how his message was typed. This is a self-correcting
   feedback loop: if a message is mis-derived, the only person who can catch it sees it
   immediately.

2. **Stamp `meta.derived_kind` on the message.** Free — the UI already stamps `meta`. This
   makes the derivation decision auditable: any consumer (runner, doctor, trace) can see how
   the kind was derived without guessing.

## Implementation surface

One file: `scripts/bifrost_ui.py`.

- New function: `_derive_user_kind(text, to, fidelity, broadcast) -> str` (~15 lines)
- Changed line 444: `kind = _derive_user_kind(text, to, fidelity, broadcast)` replaces the
  existing `kind = "inform" if fidelity=="inform" else "chat"`
- Result dict: add `"derived_kind": kind`
- Meta stamp: add `meta["derived_kind"] = kind` before the send call

Revert: restore the one line. Pin surface: ~6 pins (one per ladder row + broadcast +
mis-derivation safety + echo).

## Gate items for Daniel

| # | Decision | Recommendation |
|---|----------|---------------|
| Q1 | Kind: `question` or re-point `reply` seam? | `question` — leave clarify-answer seam untouched. `question` is already in KIND_LANE, ANSWERABLE, and all bus_send_kinds. |
| Q2 | `meta.expects_reply` needed? | No — `expectations.arm()` is test-only for user sends; kind-alone is sufficient |
| Q3 | Imperative→request row? | DROPPED — too fragile, mis-derivation cost is high |
| Q4 | Echo derived_kind to UI? | YES — self-correcting feedback loop |
| — | Stamp meta.derived_kind? | YES — provenance auditable for free |
| — | Regex breadth | Question-word prefix regex + `?` suffix — catches "Can you review this" without question mark |

body:
analysis. Supersedes the header of `research/reviewed/deepseek-w5-heal-design-2026-07-16.md`.
Reconciler: claude (Opus 4.8). SAFETY-CRITICAL slice — full-fence tier.

## The empirical finding that reframes W5 (claude's independent contribution)

DeepSeek's half designed a roster of ephemeral-transport prefixes (allowlist → quiet). Correct
as far as it goes — but I ran the **actual keyspace census** before trusting any memory-based
roster, and it changes the shape of the problem.

`check_drift` (core/foundation/store.py:789) computes `missing_in_file = redis_keys − file_keys`
over the **HybridStore's own two backends**. But that Redis instance is **shared** by every
subsystem. So `missing_in_file` is really "every Redis key the Store's File backend doesn't have"
— which is three very different things, not one:

Actual census of the 4867 "orphans" (py check_drift, grouped by family):

| Class | Families (count) | Truth |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Ephemeral transport/control/telemetry** | bifrost:work 58, inbox 18, cursor 17, generation 17, turn_metrics 114, delta 61, presence/runner/lock/expect/trace…, + drill namespaces (rb25* , bifrost_t039a*/t045* ~hundreds) | never durable anywhere — correctly Redis-only |
| **2. Store-managed DURABLE families, Redis-ahead** | events:raw 2383, narr:beat 780, learn:experiment 191, mem:decisions, recall:use, lookback, knowledge_map | **the bulk (~3500).** These families ARE in File (File owns events:raw 1761, narr:beat 339, learn:experiment 91…) — Redis just has *more*. Durable-family drift, not unknown orphans |
| **3. True unknowns** | (whatever matches neither) | the real "investigate NOW" signal |

**Why deepseek's roster-only design is insufficient (the adversarial finding):** it quiets Class 1
(~a few hundred). Class 2 — the ~3500-key bulk — is NOT ephemeral, so the allowlist correctly
leaves it LOUD… which means the heal *still* cries "3500 orphans — a write that never reached the
durable side" about **durable knowledge families**. That's not just noise, it reads as data-loss.
The wolf-cry isn't fixed; it's made scarier. The census is what surfaces this — memory wouldn't.

## The reconciled design — 3-way classification (not binary)

`heal_report` classifies each `missing_in_file` key into exactly one of three buckets, using two
sources of truth that already exist:

1. **Ephemeral roster** (deepseek's half, adopted + credited) — explicit allowlist in
   `packet_spec.py` (R6 roster home) of families that are EXPECTED Redis-only from the Store's
   view: bus transport, presence/liveness, control/coord, telemetry, durable-elsewhere subsystems
   the Store doesn't own (coord:ledger, incarnation), and drill namespaces. → **quiet count line.**
2. **Store-managed durable families** — derived automatically from `self._file.keys("*")` (the
   families the Store actually owns durably). A key whose family is in File but is Redis-only =
   **durable-family drift** → **visible, calm** line: "N durable-family keys Redis-ahead (events,
   narr, learn…) — expected for append/TTL-trimmed families; investigate if growing." Self-
   configuring: no hand-maintained list of durable families, it reads the File key-space.
3. **Neither** → **LOUD** "UNKNOWN Redis-only key(s) — investigate" (today's behavior, but now
   only for genuine unknowns, not the whole 4867).

### Safety invariants (deepseek's, preserved + extended)

- Allowlist, never denylist: a family in NO bucket-1/2 source stays LOUD (Class 3). Never hide one.
- Fail-open: roster import fails OR `_file.keys()` raises → every orphan flagged LOUD (today's
  behavior). A broken classifier can only make the heal *louder*, never quieter.
- File is truth: a key that (impossibly) matches the roster but also lives in File is treated as
  Class 2 (durable), not silenced.
- Durable-family drift is VISIBLE, not hidden: the calm line still prints the count + top families,
  so an operator can spot an abnormal spike (fsck "lost+found is visible" principle) — it is not
  suppressed, only de-escalated from "INVESTIGATE" to "expected-ish, watch if growing".

## Open questions — resolved

1. **fnmatch globs vs literal prefixes?** — fnmatch. The census proves the need: `agent:*:events`
   and drill families like `bifrost_t039a_*:trace` have mid-string wildcards a prefix `startswith`
   can't express. Cost is a non-issue: heal runs once per boot; compile-once the patterns.
2. **Modify check_drift or only heal_report?** — heal_report only. `check_drift` stays the raw
   backend-diff (pure data, other callers untouched); classification is the interpretation layer.
3. **INFO line format?** — three lines, most-severe first: UNKNOWN (loud) → durable-drift (calm,
   top families + counts) → ephemeral (quiet count). Each carries a drill where actionable.
4. **is_trace_kind ride-along?** — ALREADY LANDED in the W4 commit (packet_spec.is_trace_kind on
   origin). Moot; deepseek should pull.

## A real finding this surfaces (not silenced — the point of W5)

Class 2 is ~3500 keys of durable knowledge (events:raw +2383, narr:beat +780, learn:experiment
+191) that are in Redis but not the Store's File backend. Most likely retention-lag /
append-heavy families where Redis holds more than the last File snapshot — but the magnitude
warrants a look. W5's calm line makes this **visible and watchable** instead of buried in a
4867-key wall. → propose follow-up **T082: audit durable-family Redis↔File drift** (is events:raw
File persistence lagging, or is check_drift's per-key granularity mismatched to how the event log
compacts?). W5 does NOT fix that — it makes it legible, which is the honest-heal contract.

## Build (claude lane; deepseek cross-verifies)

- `core/comm/packet_spec.py`: `EPHEMERAL_PREFIXES` tuple (fnmatch patterns, `{ns}` resolved at
  match time) + `is_ephemeral_key(key, ns)` helper. Empirically grounded from the census above.
- `core/foundation/store.py` `heal_report`: the 3-way classification, fail-open, family-grouped
  counts. `check_drift` untouched.
- Pins (deepseek's 8 adopted + claude additions for the durable-drift class):
  W5-P1 ephemeral→quiet · W5-P2 unknown→loud · W5-P3 file-family key→durable-drift not unknown ·
  W5-P4 durable-drift line present+calm · W5-P5 roster import fails→all loud (fail-open) ·
  W5-P6 allowlist gap→loud · W5-P7 in-sync→quiet · W5-P8 counts reconcile (ephemeral+durable+unknown
  == total, lossless) · W5-P9 durable family derived from _file (self-configuring) ·
  W5-P10 fnmatch mid-wildcard (agent:*:events) classified.

Nothing builds to `done` until deepseek cross-verifies the 3-way (especially: does the durable-
drift de-escalation ever hide a Class-3 unknown? — the one safety question to hammer).

# Visual-generation repo sweep -- web agent verification report (verbatim)

Context: Daniel supplied an LLM-generated list of AI presentation/chart/diagram repos plus
philholden/partialupdate (real-time UI updates) with the directive "integrate the best
aspects into our work". A fenced web agent verified every claim against the GitHub API +
READMEs on 2026-07-09. Companion report: deepseek integration seams (same date). Preserved
verbatim below; reconciliation in docs/visual-gen-integration-2026-07.md.

---

# GitHub Project Verification Report -- 2026-07-09

Method: every repo checked against the GitHub API (existence, stars, license, last push) + README fetched from the actual repo. Verdict up front: **all 10 paths exist -- no hallucinated repos.** Two are unusable anyway (no license / no code), and several claims needed correction.

## Per-repo findings

**1. philholden/partialupdate -- EXISTS (priority assessment)**
- (a) Actually: a multi-user AI chat that generates and edits its own UI (HTML/CSS/JS) on the fly, built on Chrome's new **Declarative Partial Updates** spec -- LLM streams `<template for="name">` fragments that patch DOM at `<?marker name="...">` insertion points; forms submit structured data back into LLM context.
- (b) MIT. (c) TypeScript on **Cloudflare Workers + Durable Objects + hibernatable WebSockets** (not a plain server); needs Cloudflare account + AI Gateway. (d) 18 stars, created 2026-06-26 (two weeks old), pushed 2026-06-27. A fresh demo, not infrastructure.
- (e) Steal: the **declarative patch protocol** -- server streams named HTML fragments; browser applies them at markers with zero client framework. Its spec.md documents a clean delimiter-based message format with server-side routing props (include/exclude client ids) -- directly maps to Bifrost fidelity-ladder routing.
- (f) Rewrite-idea-only. Hard dependency: the underlying spec is **Chrome 148+ behind the experimental-web-platform flag only** (confirmed via developer.chrome.com); polyfills exist (`template-for-polyfill`, `html-setters-polyfill`). For your Python+SSE console, the production-grade equivalent that works today in every browser is **datastar** or **htmx's SSE extension** (see shortlist).

**2. presenton/presenton -- EXISTS, claims check out**
- (a) Self-hosted AI presentation generator **and REST API** (Gamma alternative). (b) Apache-2.0 (matches Aurora's). (c) Next.js frontend + **FastAPI backend** (verified `servers/fastapi` + `servers/nextjs` in tree), single Docker image, also desktop apps; providers: Ollama, LM Studio, OpenAI, Gemini, Anthropic, Bedrock, any OpenAI-compatible. Exports **editable PPTX** + PDF. Has a **built-in MCP server**. (d) ~9.0k stars, pushed 2026-07-09 (today) -- actively maintained.
- (e) Steal: run as Docker sidecar and hit its **generation API / MCP** -- templates are plain HTML+Tailwind, so agents can author custom deck templates as code.
- (f) Drop-in service (docker compose). Heaviest footprint of the good options.

**3. allweonedev/presentation-ai -- EXISTS, claim overstated**
- (a) Open-source Gamma-alternative presentation generator with outline-first workflow, 38 themes, live slide build, PPTX export. "Fully local" is **not accurate**: requires PostgreSQL, Google OAuth (NextAuth), and optional cloud keys (Together, FAL, Tavily, UploadThing); local models possible via Ollama/LM Studio but the app itself is a SaaS-shaped Next.js+Prisma stack. (b) MIT. (c) Next.js/React/Postgres/Plate editor; self-host node server. (d) ~2.9k stars, pushed 2026-06-05, maintained.
- (e) Steal: the **outline-first workflow** (generate outline -> human edits -> then render slides) -- the right UX for chronicle->deck.
- (f) Heavy self-host; realistically idea-only for you.

**4. ysskrishna/ai-ppt-slide-generator -- EXISTS, claims accurate**
- (a) Backend-only FastAPI service that turns a topic (or user-supplied slide JSON) into PPTX via Gemini + python-pptx, with configurable layouts/fonts/colors. (b) MIT. (c) Python 3.12/FastAPI/Postgres/Docker; pure API, no UI. (d) 20 stars, pushed 2025-12-27; small portfolio project, low bus-factor.
- (e) Steal: the minimal **JSON-slide-spec -> python-pptx renderer** pattern (layout types: title/bullet + config object) -- maps 1:1 to a `deck_renderer.py` inside Aurora with zero Node dependency.
- (f) Library-pattern; re-implement in an afternoon rather than adopt its Postgres.

**5. cobacha/ppt-agent -- EXISTS, claims accurate but unproven**
- (a) Text/URL -> animated slides in ~30s; FastAPI + Next.js; Anthropic API; 18 themes; exports a **single self-contained HTML file** (all CSS/JS inline, offline, grid overview on 'G'), plus PDF; SQLite history, rate limiting, per-slide regeneration, design-check auto-retry. (b) MIT. (c) Docker compose self-host. (d) **1 star**, created 2026-05-25, pushed 2026-06-12 -- brand-new, zero community.
- (e) Steal: **single-file HTML deck export** + the quality-gate auto-retry loop ("slides that fail design checks get regenerated") -- that's your "trust the gates" philosophy applied to rendering.
- (f) Drop-in service technically, but 1-star maturity risk; safest as idea/template source.

**6. yujisatojr/chart-agent -- EXISTS, stale and unlicensed**
- (a) Chatbot that generates simple charts (React + Chart.js + FastAPI + GPT-4o). (b) **NO LICENSE** -- cannot copy code into an Apache-2.0 repo. (c) React client + FastAPI server, dev-mode only. (d) 13 stars, last push 2024-06-29 -- abandoned ~2 years.
- (e) Steal (idea-only): LLM emits a Chart.js config JSON, client renders it -- trivial to re-implement.
- (f) Idea-only (license blocks anything more).

**7. thongekchakrit/ChartAI -- EXISTS, dead and unlicensed**
- (a) GPT-3-era Streamlit app: upload CSV, chat, text-to-SQL, draggable Nivo charts. (b) **NO LICENSE.** (c) Streamlit single app. (d) 78 stars, last push 2023-06-16 -- dead 3 years.
- (e)/(f) Nothing worth taking that isn't done better elsewhere; idea-only. The sole repo under topic `generative-chart` is its modern successor: **OpenVizAI/OpenVizAI** (43 stars, pushed 2026-05-10, "AI picks the chart type and fields -- JavaScript does the rest").

**8. Cocoon-AI/architecture-diagram-generator -- EXISTS, claims accurate**
- (a) Not an app: a **packaged Claude skill** (zip + prompt/templates) that makes Claude emit dark-themed architecture diagrams as standalone HTML/SVG files with built-in Copy/PNG/PDF export buttons and semantic color coding per component type. (b) MIT. (c) HTML templates + skill definition; runs wherever Claude runs. (d) ~6.4k stars, created 2025-12-22, pushed 2026-05-13.
- (e) Steal: the **self-contained HTML/SVG diagram template** (embedded export buttons, slate-950 theme, arrows-behind-boxes layering) -- lift it as Aurora's visual-report house style, or just install the skill in Claude Code as-is.
- (f) Drop-in (it literally targets Claude; zero integration code).

**9. DayuanJiang/next-ai-draw-io -- EXISTS, claims accurate; the giant of the list**
- (a) Next.js app embedding draw.io: AI generates/modifies **draw.io XML** from natural language, streamed live onto the canvas (Vercel AI SDK + react-drawio); multi-provider; desktop app; Docker. (b) Apache-2.0. (c) Self-host node/Docker, or hosted demo; plus a published **MCP server**: `claude mcp add drawio -- npx @next-ai-drawio/mcp-server@latest` -- diagrams appear in the browser in real time. (d) ~33k stars, pushed 2026-07-09 (today) -- very actively maintained.
- (e) Steal: the **MCP server + draw.io-XML-as-artifact** design -- diagrams are durable, editable, versionable XML (Ledger-friendly), not opaque PNGs.
- (f) Drop-in (one MCP add for agent use; Docker for full app).

**10. graphic-design-ai/creatiposter -- EXISTS but is a PAPER STUB**
- (a) ByteDance's CreatiPoster (arXiv 2506.10890): multi-layer editable AI graphic composition. **No code, no model checkpoint, no license** -- the README's own to-do list still shows "publish codebase" unchecked; language=null; last push 2025-06-14. (d) 100 stars. (f) **Unusable** -- bookmark and revisit only if they ship. No verified open-source equivalent at its game; the practical route for editable visual compositions today is HTML/SVG generation (item 8's approach).

## Topic sweeps (verified via API)
- `topic:presentation-maker` -- junk drawer; top hit SlideAI (156 stars, dead since 2023). Nothing here beats your list.
- `topic:generative-chart` -- exactly one repo: OpenVizAI (above).
- No dominant "awesome presentation tools" list exists; search returns noise.

**Three standouts that beat the listed repos at their own game** (all verified today):
- **starfederation/datastar** -- 4.6k stars, MIT, pushed 2026-07-08. SSE-native hypermedia framework: any backend (your Python server) streams HTML-fragment patch events; a single small JS file applies them. Beats partialupdate at its own game, in all browsers, today.
- **yuzutech/kroki** -- 4.2k stars, MIT, pushed 2026-07-08. Self-hosted Docker service: one HTTP API turning Mermaid/PlantUML/Graphviz/D2/Excalidraw text into SVG/PNG. Beats every AI-diagram app at deterministic, server-side, token-free rendering. (mermaid itself: 89k stars, MIT, active -- one `<script>` tag renders diagrams client-side inside your console.)
- **slidevjs/slidev** -- 47.6k stars, MIT, pushed 2026-07-03. Markdown -> developer-grade slides/PDF/hosted deck. For chronicle->deck, an agent writing markdown + slidev rendering beats AI-layout tools on determinism and cost. (Lighter headless option: marp-team/marp-cli, 3.7k stars, MIT, pushed today -- md -> PPTX/PDF/HTML in one CLI call.)

## Ranked shortlist (value-to-effort for your three goals)

1. **datastar (or htmx+SSE extension)** -- goal (i). Keep your existing SSE channel; change payloads from "poll signal" to "HTML fragment + target selector"; DOM updates in place, no reloads, no polling, no build step, works in every browser. Library drop-in against the current Python console. Take partialupdate's routing idea (include/exclude client ids per fragment) for per-agent console views; skip its Chrome-flag dependency.
2. **next-ai-draw-io MCP server** -- goal (ii). One `claude mcp add` and agents produce live, editable architecture/flow diagrams; store the draw.io XML as atoms so diagrams are regenerable projections, not screenshots. 33k stars, Apache-2.0, pushed today -- the safest big bet on the list.
3. **kroki (+ mermaid in-console)** -- goal (ii) cheap tier. Docker sidecar next to Redis; `POST text -> SVG` lets any agent render diagrams deterministically with zero LLM tokens (token-frugality directive). Mermaid script-tag in the console renders those same text specs live inside SSE-patched panels.
4. **marp-cli or slidev** -- goal (iii) cheap tier. Chronicle/notes are already markdown-shaped; one CLI call yields a shareable HTML/PPTX/PDF deck, deterministic and reviewable in git. Steal Cocoon's self-contained-HTML-with-export-buttons template as the house style for one-page visual reports.
5. **presenton** -- goal (iii) full tier, when you want AI-designed editable PPTX for external optics: Apache-2.0 Docker sidecar with REST API + MCP, works against Ollama. Adopt only if the marp/slidev tier proves insufficient -- it is the heaviest item that still earns its place.

Licensing hazards to record: chart-agent and ChartAI have no license (ideas only, never copy code); creatiposter has no code at all.
